paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend. When David realizes what he has done, he doesn't hide behind anybody. He says, "I have sinned greatly because I have done this thing" (1 Chronicles 21:8). Later he says, "I am the one who has sinned and acted wickedly" (1 Chronicles 21:17). No excuses, no "well, technically." Owning it plainly is the first step back to God.

Now look at where David runs when it all goes wrong. He tells Gad, "Please, let me fall into the hand of the LORD, for His mercies are very great" (1 Chronicles 21:13). Then the LORD sees the destruction, relents, and says, "Enough! Withdraw your hand now!" (1 Chronicles 21:15). I think that tells us where to turn when we mess up: toward God, not away from Him. His mercies are bigger than my worst day, and I had some REAL bad days in that drawer.

Then there's the altar, and this part is for you and me. David could take the threshing floor for free, but he says, "I will not take for the LORD what belongs to you, nor will I offer burnt offerings that cost me nothing" (1 Chronicles 21:24). Worship that costs us something shows that we mean it. So ask yourself, baker: what am I willing to give to God today, and not just the leftovers? And this story keeps pointing to mercy, because the LORD answered David with fire from heaven (1 Chronicles 21:26).
